body.en: A *binary* tree is a set of nodes in which each node has at most two children, called the left and right child. The top node is the root; a node with no children is a leaf (external node); other nodes are internal. Nodes with the same parent are siblings. The depth (level) of a node is the number of edges from the root (root at level 0); the height of the tree is the largest depth. The size is the number of nodes. A binary tree of height h has at most 2^(h+1) − 1 nodes, and level k has at most 2^k nodes.

body.en: A *binary search* tree (BST) is a binary tree in which, for every node, all keys in the left subtree are smaller and all keys in the right subtree are larger. To search, start at the root and go left or right by comparing, so a balanced BST of n nodes is searched in about log2 n steps. An inorder traversal of a BST visits the keys in ascending order. Inserting keys in sorted order makes the tree degenerate into a chain, as slow as a list.

say.en: Insert 45, 25, 65, 15, 35, 55 into an empty BST and give its inorder and preorder traversals.
45 is the root. 25 is less than 45 gives left; 65 is greater than 45 gives right.
15 is less than 45, is less than 25 gives left of 25; 35 is less than 45, is greater than 25 gives right of 25.
55 is greater than 45, is less than 65 gives left of 65.
Inorder: 15 25 35 45 55 65 sorted. Preorder: 45 25 15 35 65 55.
So the answer is Inorder 15 25 35 45 55 65; preorder 45 25 15 35 65 55.
